cards.front: Single progesterone samples from normally cycling women in the mid-to-late luteal phase spanned 2.3 to 40.1 ng per mL, and both ends came from healthy women. What does that span show about the corpus luteum?
cards.back: Its output is not steady. Progesterone also swung widely within single 24-hour profiles, so the gland is secreting in episodes rather than at a constant rate.
cards.why: The pooled span mixes different women and sampling times, so the within-day swing is the part that argues against a steady gland.
cards.quote: a gland whose output moves that much within a day is not running at a steady rate

cards.front: The ovary holds a fixed reserve of {{c1::primordial}} follicles, each an oocyte with a single flat layer of granulosa cells.
cards.quote: The ovary holds a fixed reserve of primordial follicles, each an oocyte with a single flat layer of granulosa cells
cards.section: Most follicles die; one is chosen

cards.front: In the adult human ovary, how does initial recruitment of follicles differ from cyclic recruitment?
cards.back: Initial recruitment moves primordial follicles into growth continuously, from before puberty on, and does not need the cycle's FSH. Cyclic recruitment acts months later, on small antral follicles, and depends on rising FSH.
cards.quote: Initial recruitment moves primordial follicles into growth continuously, from before puberty on, and does not depend on the cycle's FSH.
cards.section: Most follicles die; one is chosen

cards.front: In the human model, rising FSH rescues a cohort of small antral follicles from {{c1::atresia}}, the degeneration that ends almost every follicle.
cards.quote: rising FSH rescues a cohort of small antral follicles from atresia, the degeneration that ends almost every follicle
cards.section: Most follicles die; one is chosen

cards.front: Why does FSH rise at the end of one cycle, in time to rescue the next cohort of small antral follicles?
cards.back: The ovarian brake is lifted. As the corpus luteum regresses, estradiol, progesterone and inhibin A fall, and FSH rises as that negative feedback is withdrawn.
cards.quote: as the corpus luteum regresses, estradiol, progesterone and inhibin A fall, and with that brake lifted FSH rises
cards.section: Most follicles die; one is chosen

cards.front: In the human cycle, which cells make inhibin B, and what does it do at the pituitary?
cards.back: Granulosa cells of the rescued follicles make it; it is a granulosa-cell protein that suppresses pituitary FSH secretion.
cards.quote: The rescued follicles then make estradiol and inhibin B, a granulosa-cell protein that suppresses pituitary FSH secretion.
cards.section: Most follicles die; one is chosen

cards.front: Through the mid-follicular phase of the human cycle, is inhibin B or estradiol the main brake on FSH, and why?
cards.back: Estradiol. Inhibin B peaks just after the intercycle FSH rise and then falls, so the rising estradiol from the cohort carries the brake through the mid-follicular phase.
cards.quote: Inhibin B peaks just after the intercycle FSH rise and then falls, so rising estradiol is the main brake through the mid-follicular phase.
cards.section: Most follicles die; one is chosen

cards.front: As FSH falls through the mid-follicular phase, what decides which follicle of the cohort becomes dominant?
cards.back: FSH responsiveness, the acquisition of granulosa LH receptors, and local growth support together. The rest undergo atresia.
cards.why: The cohort lowers the very hormone that saved it, so survival goes to the follicle that still clears its own FSH threshold and can also use LH.
cards.quote: FSH responsiveness, the acquisition of granulosa LH receptors and local growth support together decide which one.
cards.section: Most follicles die; one is chosen

cards.front: In normally ovulating women, FSH was raised either as a brief early rise or as a moderate rise sustained into the mid-to-late follicular phase. What happened to the number of growing follicles, and what does the contrast support?
cards.back: The brief rise did not maintain extra follicles; the sustained moderate rise let several follicles keep growing. That supports an FSH window: selection depends on how long FSH stays above each follicle's threshold, not on the threshold alone.
cards.quote: A brief early rise did not maintain extra follicles; a moderate rise sustained into the mid-to-late follicular phase let several follicles keep growing.
cards.section: Most follicles die; one is chosen

cards.front: The two-arm FSH study in ovulating women supports an FSH window. Why can it not be used to name one FSH threshold value for follicle survival?
cards.back: The arms differed in timing as well as duration, so the comparison cannot separate the two, and the study does not define one threshold value.
cards.quote: The arms differed in timing as well as duration, so the study does not define one threshold value.
cards.section: Most follicles die; one is chosen

cards.front: In 50 women scanned by transvaginal ultrasound every day for one interovulatory interval, how many waves of follicle growth were seen, and how often?
cards.back: Two waves in 68 percent of women and three in 32 percent. Only the last wave of an interval ended in ovulation.
cards.quote: found two waves of follicle growth in 68 percent and three in 32 percent
cards.section: Most follicles die; one is chosen

cards.front: A student says follicular waves mean a woman can ovulate two or three times in one interovulatory interval. Correct the claim and say how settled the wave model is.
cards.back: A wave is a synchronous round of antral follicle growth, not an extra ovulation, and in that study only the last wave of an interval ended in ovulation. The wave model is a proposal from that ultrasound study and is still debated.
cards.quote: The wave model is a proposal from this study and is still debated; a wave is a round of growth, not an extra ovulation.
cards.section: Most follicles die; one is chosen

cards.front: In the human preovulatory follicle, theca cells sit outside the basement membrane and carry LH receptors and {{c1::CYP17}}, the enzyme that turns pregnane steroids into androgens.
cards.back: In isolated human theca cells, androstenedione was the main steroid measured.
cards.quote: Theca cells, outside the membrane, carry LH receptors and CYP17 (17-alpha-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase), the enzyme that turns pregnane steroids into androgens.
cards.section: Two cells, two gonadotropins, one estrogen

cards.front: Granulosa cells, inside the basement membrane, carry FSH receptors and {{c1::aromatase (CYP19A1)}}, the enzyme that converts androgens to estrogens.
cards.back: FSH raises granulosa-cell aromatase.
cards.quote: Granulosa cells, inside, carry FSH receptors and aromatase (CYP19A1), the enzyme that converts androgens to estrogens, and FSH raises their aromatase.
cards.section: Two cells, two gonadotropins, one estrogen

cards.front: Trace the androgen made by human theca cells to the follicle's main secreted estrogen.
cards.back: Androstenedione crosses the basement membrane to the granulosa cells, where aromatase converts it to estrone and testosterone to estradiol; a 17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase interconverts the pairs, and estradiol is the main secreted estrogen.
cards.quote: Androstenedione crosses to the granulosa cells, where aromatase converts it to estrone, and testosterone to estradiol
cards.section: Two cells, two gonadotropins, one estrogen

cards.front: A drug that blocks aromatase is given to a woman in the mid-follicular phase. Predict what happens to follicular estradiol and to FSH, and why.
cards.back: Estradiol falls and FSH rises. Granulosa aromatase is the step that makes estrogen from theca androgen, so blocking it removes the follicle's estradiol output, and estradiol is the main brake on FSH through the mid-follicular phase.
cards.quote: Granulosa cells, inside, carry FSH receptors and aromatase (CYP19A1), the enzyme that converts androgens to estrogens, and FSH raises their aromatase.
cards.section: Two cells, two gonadotropins, one estrogen

cards.front: Theca-cell CYP17 is inhibited in a growing human follicle while FSH and granulosa aromatase stay normal. Predict the effect on estradiol output and why.
cards.back: Estradiol output falls. CYP17 makes the androgen that granulosa cells aromatize, so the granulosa compartment is left with no substrate even though its enzyme is intact.
cards.why: In the two-cell model the two layers share one pathway, so losing either station stops the product.
cards.quote: Theca cells, outside the membrane, carry LH receptors and CYP17 (17-alpha-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase), the enzyme that turns pregnane steroids into androgens.
cards.section: Two cells, two gonadotropins, one estrogen

cards.front: How does the two-cell, two-gonadotropin model account for the end of follicle selection, when FSH is falling?
cards.back: As granulosa cells differentiate under FSH they acquire functional LH receptors, so the most mature follicle responds to LH as well as FSH and keeps growing and making estradiol while FSH falls. Smaller follicles have not gained that LH responsiveness.
cards.quote: as granulosa cells differentiate under FSH, they acquire functional LH receptors
cards.section: Two cells, two gonadotropins, one estrogen

cards.front: Across a human cycle, what does inhibin B report on, and what does inhibin A report on?
cards.back: Inhibin B tracks the growing cohort of small antral follicles, rising rapidly in the early follicular phase; inhibin A tracks the active corpus luteum and reaches its maximum in the midluteal phase.
cards.quote: inhibin B tracks the growing cohort of small antral follicles, inhibin A the active corpus luteum
cards.section: Two cells, two gonadotropins, one estrogen

cards.front: Twelve postmenopausal women, whose ovaries make little estradiol, were given estradiol. What happened to LH pulse frequency, and what does that show?
cards.back: LH pulse frequency slowed within 24 hours, showing that estradiol alone acts as a negative feedback signal on pulsatile LH release. Progesterone was not manipulated in that study.
cards.quote: when estradiol was restored, LH pulse frequency slowed within 24 hours
cards.section: From brake to accelerator: the switch to positive feedback

cards.front: Slower LH pulses after estradiol are read as slower GnRH pulses in women. Why is that an inference rather than a measurement?
cards.back: Each LH pulse is thought to follow a GnRH pulse, but GnRH in portal blood cannot be sampled in women, so the hypothalamic pulse is never measured directly.
cards.quote: GnRH in portal blood cannot be sampled in women
cards.section: From brake to accelerator: the switch to positive feedback

cards.front: Late in the follicular phase, when estradiol from the dominant follicle stays high for long enough, it becomes {{c1::positive feedback}}, a signal that raises its own trigger, and LH climbs steeply in the surge.
cards.quote: when estradiol from the dominant follicle stays high for long enough, it becomes positive feedback, a signal that raises its own trigger
cards.section: From brake to accelerator: the switch to positive feedback

cards.front: In the human cycle, how fast does the LH surge rise, how long does it last, and where does its onset sit relative to ovulation?
cards.back: In women sampled every 2 hours, LH doubled within 2 hours of onset and the surge lasted about 48 hours on average. Textbooks place onset roughly 34 to 36 hours before ovulation, with individual intervals varying widely.
cards.quote: Textbooks place surge onset roughly 34 to 36 hours before ovulation, and individual intervals vary widely.
cards.section: From brake to accelerator: the switch to positive feedback

cards.front: Asked for the estradiol concentration and duration that flip feedback from negative to positive in women, what is the honest answer?
cards.back: No single level or duration can be given, because quoted values differ between sources. The requirement is that estradiol stays high long enough, not a stated number.
cards.quote: No single estradiol level or duration for the switch is given here, because quoted values differ between sources.
cards.section: From brake to accelerator: the switch to positive feedback

cards.front: Why is estradiol's effect on the surge thought to reach GnRH neurons indirectly, and which neurons are the leading candidates?
cards.back: In rodents GnRH neurons carry little or no estrogen receptor alpha, so the signal is thought to pass through other neurons. Kisspeptin neurons are the leading candidates, acting on GnRH neurons through KISS1R, a G protein-coupled receptor.
cards.quote: In rodents, GnRH neurons carry little or no estrogen receptor alpha (ERalpha), so the signal is thought to pass through other neurons.
cards.section: From brake to accelerator: the switch to positive feedback

cards.front: What is the reproductive phenotype of people carrying loss-of-function mutations in KISS1R?
cards.back: They fail to enter puberty normally, which is the human evidence that kisspeptin signalling through KISS1R is needed.
cards.quote: people with loss-of-function KISS1R mutations fail to enter puberty normally
cards.section: From brake to accelerator: the switch to positive feedback

cards.front: Estrogen receptor alpha was deleted from kisspeptin-expressing cells in female mice. After ovariectomy, estradiol regimens producing either negative feedback or a surge were given. What was found, and what does it establish?
cards.back: Estradiol still lowered mean LH in the knockouts, but they made no LH surge. In that mouse paradigm, kisspeptin-cell ERalpha is required for the estradiol-induced surge and is not the only route for suppression.
cards.quote: Estradiol still lowered mean LH in the knockouts, but they made no LH surge.
cards.section: From brake to accelerator: the switch to positive feedback

cards.front: Two things the kisspeptin-cell ERalpha knockout cannot settle about the LH surge. Name them.
cards.back: Whether the receptor is needed during development or in adulthood, since the deletion was present from development and confounds the two; and which kisspeptin population matters, since both AVPV and arcuate cells lost the receptor.
cards.why: It is also a mouse result: in women the surge circuitry is less well localized, so the rodent AVPV pathway cannot be stated as the human mechanism.
cards.quote: The deletion was present from development, so developmental and adult signaling requirements are confounded
cards.section: From brake to accelerator: the switch to positive feedback

cards.front: A woman takes a contraceptive-type steroid preparation that holds estradiol and progesterone at a steady level through the cycle, acting as sustained negative feedback. Predict whether an LH surge and ovulation occur, and why.
cards.back: Neither occurs. The surge needs the late-follicular switch to positive feedback; sustained steroid negative feedback on GnRH and LH release blocks it. This is one way hormonal contraception prevents ovulation.
cards.quote: sustained steroid negative feedback blocks the surge
cards.section: From brake to accelerator: the switch to positive feedback

cards.front: Name the three things the LH surge does to the follicle and its oocyte.
cards.back: It restarts meiosis in the oocyte, turns the granulosa and theca cells into luteal cells, and leads to rupture of the follicle wall.
cards.quote: The surge restarts meiosis in the oocyte, turns the granulosa and theca cells into luteal cells, and leads to rupture of the follicle wall.
cards.section: Ovulation and a corpus luteum that pulses

cards.front: In follicle-enclosed mouse oocytes, what chain of molecules holds meiosis arrested before LH, and what does LH change?
cards.back: Granulosa cGMP passes into the oocyte through gap junctions and inhibits PDE3A, the oocyte's cAMP-degrading phosphodiesterase, so cAMP stays high and meiosis stays arrested. LH acts on the somatic cells, lowers their cGMP and closes the gap junctions, so oocyte cGMP and then cAMP fall and meiosis resumes.
cards.why: The stimulus goes to the somatic cells; what the oocyte sees is the withdrawal of an inhibitor of an inhibitor.
cards.quote: Before LH, cGMP made in the granulosa cells passes into the oocyte through gap junctions and inhibits PDE3A
cards.section: Ovulation and a corpus luteum that pulses

cards.front: A follicle-enclosed mouse oocyte is given LH together with a drug that inhibits PDE3A inside the oocyte. Predict oocyte cAMP and whether meiosis resumes, and say which rule the prediction rests on.
cards.back: cAMP stays high and meiosis stays arrested. The rule is that LH works by lowering oocyte cGMP, which relieves inhibition of PDE3A so that PDE3A degrades cAMP; blocking the enzyme that must be released prevents the cAMP fall the lesson describes.
cards.quote: what the oocyte sees is the withdrawal of an inhibitor of an inhibitor
cards.section: Ovulation and a corpus luteum that pulses

cards.front: After the follicle ruptures, which cells form the corpus luteum, and what does it secrete?
cards.back: Luteinized granulosa cells and theca-lutein cells form it. It secretes progesterone and, in the midluteal phase, a second rise of estradiol; progesterone slows LH pulse frequency.
cards.quote: luteinized granulosa cells and theca-lutein cells form the corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone and, in the midluteal phase, a second rise of estradiol
cards.section: Ovulation and a corpus luteum that pulses

cards.front: Normally cycling women in separate early, middle and late luteal groups had blood drawn every 10 minutes for 24 hours. What happened to LH pulse frequency and to progesterone, and what does that rule in?
cards.back: LH pulse frequency fell from a mean of 15.2 to 8.4 pulses per 24 hours between the early and late groups, and in the mid and late luteal phase progesterone was episodic, rising after LH pulses. That rules in a corpus luteum under pulsatile pituitary control.
cards.quote: LH pulse frequency fell across the luteal phase, from a mean of 15.2 to 8.4 pulses per 24 hours between the early and late groups.
cards.section: The classic experiment: Filicori, Butler and Crowley, 1984

cards.front: In the 24-hour luteal sampling study, progesterone episodes followed LH pulses. Why can that not be called causation, and why can it not describe change within one woman?
cards.back: The evidence is timing, not blockade, so no LH pulse was shown to cause the episode after it; and each luteal phase was a different group of women, so the study cannot follow change within one woman.
cards.quote: Not shown: that each LH pulse causes the episode after it, since the evidence is timing, not blockade
cards.section: The classic experiment: Filicori, Butler and Crowley, 1984

cards.front: Group means were 15.2 LH pulses per 24 hours in the early luteal phase and 8.4 in the late luteal phase. Find each mean pulse interval, and the samples per interval if blood is drawn every 60 minutes.
cards.back: Early luteal: 1,440 / 15.2 = 94.7 min, and 94.7 / 60 = 1.6 samples per interval. Late luteal: 1,440 / 8.4 = 171.4 min, and 171.4 / 60 = 2.9 samples per interval.
cards.why: Pulse interval = 1,440 min per day divided by pulses per day; samples per interval = pulse interval divided by sampling interval.
cards.quote: Sampling every 60 minutes gives 1.6 and 2.9.
cards.section: Reading the cycle's hormone curves

cards.front: A team plans to resolve LH pulses in the early luteal phase, where the mean interval is 94.7 minutes, by sampling every 30 minutes. Calculate the samples per interval and say how much confidence the number buys.
cards.back: 94.7 / 30 = 3.2 samples per interval, above the rule of thumb of about two, so pulses can be resolved in principle. It is not a guarantee: even above that ratio peaks can fall between samples, and a design built on the group mean will undersample any woman whose pulses are faster.
cards.quote: below about two samples per interval pulses cannot be resolved, and even above it peaks can fall between samples
cards.section: Reading the cycle's hormone curves

cards.front: Predict the endocrine changes of menopause: which hormones rise and which fall, and which rises more?
cards.back: Inhibin B, inhibin A and estradiol fall as the follicle supply runs out, progesterone stays low for want of a corpus luteum, and ovarian negative feedback is largely lost, so FSH and LH rise, FSH usually by more than LH.
cards.quote: as the follicle supply runs out, inhibin B, inhibin A and estradiol fall, ovarian negative feedback is largely lost, and FSH rises, usually by more than LH
cards.section: Reading the cycle's hormone curves

cards.front: Why is the rise in FSH after menopause not fully explained by the loss of ovarian negative feedback?
cards.back: Ageing of the hypothalamus and pituitary contributes as well, so the rise is not only the loss of feedback.
cards.quote: Ageing of the hypothalamus and pituitary contributes as well, so the rise is not only the loss of feedback.
cards.section: Reading the cycle's hormone curves

cards.front: In the late follicular phase, before any surge, the dominant follicle is destroyed while the rest of the axis is intact. Predict estradiol, LH, progesterone and FSH over the following days, and name the rules you used.
cards.back: Estradiol falls, so no LH surge occurs and there is no ovulation; with no corpus luteum, progesterone does not make its post-ovulatory rise and the second estradiol rise is absent; with the ovarian brake gone, FSH rises, as it does at a cycle's end. Rules: the dominant follicle is the source of late-follicular estradiol, the surge needs sustained high estradiol, the corpus luteum forms from the ruptured follicle, and estradiol and inhibins restrain FSH.
cards.quote: progesterone begins to rise shortly before the surge and climbs after ovulation, with a second, smaller estradiol rise
cards.section: Reading the cycle's hormone curves

cards.front: To ask whether estradiol's positive feedback acts through AVPV kisspeptin neurons, arcuate kisspeptin neurons or both, the receptor must be removed in adulthood from one region's kisspeptin cells only. Why inject a guide-RNA virus into mice making Cas9 only in kisspeptin cells, rather than a Cre virus into floxed-ERalpha mice?
cards.back: Because the cell-type restriction comes from Cas9 rather than from the virus: with Cas9 made only in kisspeptin cells, a broadly infecting guide-RNA virus still edits only those cells, while a Cre virus active in any cell type would also delete the receptor in non-kisspeptin neurons near the needle.
cards.quote: With Cas9 made only in kisspeptin cells, a broadly infecting guide-RNA virus still edits only those cells.
cards.section: Design problem

cards.front: A region-restricted knockout mouse makes no LH surge. Why does that not locate the defect in kisspeptin neurons, and how do a GnRH challenge and a kisspeptin challenge narrow it down?
cards.back: Circulating LH reports the pituitary, so a lost surge could lie upstream at GnRH neurons. A GnRH challenge tests pituitary LH release; a kisspeptin challenge also tests the GnRH step, so comparing the two narrows where the defect is without proving the normal route.
cards.quote: circulating LH reports the pituitary, so a lost surge could lie upstream at GnRH neurons
cards.section: Design problem
